title: Social Media Analytics
description:
• Background Social media platforms are complex ecosystems driven by human emotion, diverse demographics, and interconnected networks. To truly understand an online community, it is required look beneath the surface. This requires understanding how followers feel (Sentiment Analysis), who those followers are (Demographics), what topics are captivating them (Trend Tracking), and how they influence one another (Link Analysis). Combining these four vectors using AI is the key to unlocking true audience intelligence.
• Description Participants will be challenged to design and build an AI-driven Social Media Analytics Framework that processes raw platform data to extract deep, actionable audience insights. The system must leverage advanced Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques to simultaneously infer follower sentiment, map audience demographics, identify top trending narratives, and perform link/network analysis to uncover how information and influence flow among followers.
• Expected Solution AI solution must address the following five core components:
A. Continuous Data Collection & Timeline Management: Design a multi-platform data ingestion pipeline capable of pulling live data, posts, user interactions, and comments. The architecture must support a structured, time-stamped historical database to map out the exact chronology of conversations. The pipeline platform requirements are categorized as follows:
• Essentials (Must-Have): X (formerly Twitter) & Telegram.
• Desirable (Good-to-Have): Instagram & Facebook.
• Appreciable Additions: Reddit or YouTube (for extracting text-based context from video comments).
B. Multi-Dimensional Sentiment Inference: Use Natural Language Processing (NLP) to detect nuanced emotions (e.g., sarcasm, anxiety, excitement, supportive, against etc.) within user posts and comment threads, mapping how these sentiments fluctuate along the established data timeline.
C. Automated Demographic Profiling: Develop models to infer aggregate, anonymized follower demographics (such as age brackets, geographic distribution, language, and professional interests) based on public profile indicators, bio text, behavioral patterns etc.
D. Real-Time Trend & Topic Detection: Automatically identify, rank, and predict rising trends, viral keywords, and shifting discussions as they emerge chronologically in the dataset.
E. Link Analysis & Network Topology: Map the relationships among followers. Identify 'nodes of high influence' (key opinion leaders) and visualize how a trend or sentiment spreads from one user segment to another over time.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, artificial intelligence, machine learning applied to a miscellaneous problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Miscellaneous. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on real-time, architecture. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 19/30 -> Yellow verdict.

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an AI framework that analyzes a social media account's followers to understand their sentiment, demographics, trending topics, and how influence flows between them, combining four analytical angles into one audience-intelligence system.
overview.why_it_matters: Understanding an online community deeply, not just surface engagement numbers, requires combining multiple analytical lenses together. A genuinely integrated system gives real audience intelligence rather than fragmented metrics.
pain_points: Social media platforms are complex, and understanding an audience requires multiple analytical angles simultaneously.
Sentiment, demographics, trends, and influence networks are typically analyzed separately, not combined.
Manual analysis across these dimensions doesn't scale to real platform data volumes.
overview.background: Understanding an online community requires combining sentiment analysis, demographic mapping, trend tracking, and link/influence analysis, but these are typically handled as separate tools rather than one integrated intelligence framework.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI-driven Social Media Analytics Framework combining continuous data ingestion, sentiment analysis, demographic inference, trend tracking, and link/network analysis into one integrated audience-intelligence system.
expected_solution: Multi-platform continuous data ingestion and timeline management.
Trend/topic tracking and link/network influence analysis.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Combining four distinct analytical capabilities (sentiment, demographics, trends, network analysis) into one coherent, integrated system is genuine, substantial technical integration.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Each analytical component individually uses established techniques; genuine effort is in meaningful integration and correlation across all four simultaneously.

competitive_landscape.note: Social media analytics tools are common generally, but genuine four-dimension integration for a government-intelligence context is more specialized than typical marketing-analytics pitches.

innovation.note: Individual components are established, genuine value is in meaningful cross-component integration and correlation.

invention.note: Building and integrating four distinct analytical capabilities together is substantial technical breadth.

technical_feasibility.note: Established NLP/sentiment, demographic-inference, and network-analysis techniques and public social media datasets support this.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine value for understanding online communities and information flow, relevant to a national-security analytical context.

architecture.note: Four analytical modules feeding an integrated dashboard, real but manageable complexity if scoped thoughtfully.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, genuinely achievable with established techniques for each component. Scope to 2-3 of the four components built genuinely well rather than shallow coverage of all four, and be thoughtful about data-collection ethics/platform terms of service.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Well-specified, concrete list of required analytical capabilities gives clear, checkable technical targets.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Attempting shallow coverage of all four components will likely produce a demo that's broad but unconvincing in any single dimension, prioritize 2-3 done genuinely well.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Prioritize sentiment analysis and trend tracking as your core (most tractable, well-supported techniques), with demographic inference and network analysis as secondary/stretch components if time allows, rather than attempting shallow coverage of all four.

idea_0_4: Source or construct sample social media data (public datasets or your own test accounts, respecting platform terms of service).
Choose your priority components: sentiment analysis and trend tracking as core, demographic/network analysis as stretch.
Split: one person on sentiment/trend analysis, one on demographic/network analysis if attempted.
prototype_4_22: Build sentiment analysis on your collected/sample data.
Start demographic inference or network/link analysis if time allows.
integration_22_30: Connect your components into one coherent dashboard.
Test with a realistic sample dataset to confirm meaningful, correlated insights across components.
Add basic cross-component correlation (e.g. sentiment trends over time linked to specific topics).
polish_30_36: Polish the dashboard for genuine analyst usability.
Rehearse a live demo showing integrated insights across your built components.
Prepare to discuss data-collection ethics and platform terms-of-service considerations.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show a genuine cross-component insight, e.g. sentiment shifting specifically around a particular trending topic, correlated with network analysis showing which accounts are driving that narrative, that integrated, correlated insight is the actual point of combining these four analytical angles.

strengths: Well-specified, concrete technical targets with established underlying techniques.
Real integration value if built with genuine cross-component correlation.
weaknesses: Full coverage of all four components at high quality isn't achievable in 36 hours, requires prioritization.
Real data collection needs careful attention to platform terms of service and ethical considerations.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced across your chosen priority components.
team_fit.approach: Prioritize sentiment and trend analysis as your reliable core, treat demographic and network analysis as stretch goals.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard sentiment analysis and topic-modeling scaffolding.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing genuine cross-component correlation that produces real, actionable insight rather than four disconnected dashboards, that's real analytical design judgment.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: Four separately AI-scaffolded components without genuine correlation design would just be four disconnected tools, not the integrated audience-intelligence system this PS asks for.

data_resource_availability.status: Public social media datasets exist for research purposes; live data collection needs to respect platform terms of service and API access policies.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Use publicly available research datasets or your own test accounts' data for a realistic but ethically sourced demonstration.

judge_qna.question: How do your different analytical components actually correlate with each other, not just run in parallel?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Show a specific example of cross-component insight, sentiment change linked to a specific trend, correlated with network analysis of who's driving it.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would this integrated insight let an analyst do that four separate tools wouldn't?

judge_qna.question: How did you source your data, and does it comply with platform terms of service?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be direct about your data source (public research datasets, or your own test accounts) and confirm you respected platform API/terms-of-service constraints during collection.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would this scale to real, larger-volume data collection while remaining compliant?
